title: Localize TreatmentCard save action labels
summary: Add an optional formatter that lets consumers localize saved and unsaved accessible labels while preserving the current Korean labels when omitted.

apiChanges.rationale: Consumers can localize both save states without replacing the button or weakening its aria-pressed contract.

implementationPlan: Add the optional formatter to TreatmentCardProps and retain the existing Korean string construction as the fallback.
Use the formatter only for the save button accessible name while keeping aria-pressed, disabled, and onSavedChange behavior unchanged.
Regenerate the component manifest and API documentation after implementation.

testCases.name: keeps default Korean labels
testCases.assertion: Without getSaveLabel, unsaved and saved buttons retain the existing Korean accessible names.

testCases.name: uses localized labels for both states
testCases.assertion: The formatter receives the current saved state and title before and after onSavedChange interactions.

testCases.name: preserves the toggle accessibility contract
testCases.assertion: The button exposes a non-empty localized accessible name, aria-pressed, and disabled state without axe violations.

documentation: Document getSaveLabel with Korean fallback and English localization examples in the generated TreatmentCard API page.
Add the localization decision and compatibility impact to the changelog.

risks.risk: A consumer formatter could return an empty label.
risks.mitigation: Validate the returned string in development and fall back to the existing Korean label when it is empty.

risks.risk: Formatter identity changes could add unnecessary render work in large lists.
risks.mitigation: Call the formatter only during render and document that consumers should pass a stable function for large collections.
